Definition: Talmai, the name of a Canaanite and a Syrian
BiblicalUsage: Talmai is the name of two men. One was a son of Anak, a giant of Hebron, whom Caleb drove out when he took the city. The other was Talmai, king of Geshur, whose daughter Maacah became David's wife and Absalom's mother, bringing a prince — and sorrow — into David's house, while the first Talmai was met by spies and driven out by Caleb.
TheologicalSignificance: One name carries two stories here, I believe: a giant driven out of Hebron, and a king whose daughter's son would rebel against his father. God works through both.
